cls: Benzoquinolizine fluoroquinolone antibacterial (anti-MRSA; S-(-)-enantiomer of nadifloxacin)
pharm: Bactericidal benzoquinolizine fluoroquinolone that preferentially inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase while retaining topoisomerase IV affinity, giving potent Gram-positive activity (including MRSA and quinolone-resistant S. aureus) with enhanced potency at acidic pH and a very low frequency of resistance.
quick: IV 800 mg q12h over 90 min; oral alalevonadifloxacin 1000 mg q12h, 7-14 days
Oral may be taken with or without food; separate from antacids/iron/zinc/sucralfate
Per-label contraindicated; presence in human milk unknown
Not established - no dedicated PK studies in renal impairment
No adjustment recommended (AUC rise <2-fold even in severe impairment)
Not addressed in labeling; general fluoroquinolone caution
Tendons, peripheral neuropathy, CNS/psychiatric status, blood glucose, diarrhea
summary: Levonadifloxacin is a novel broad-spectrum benzoquinolizine fluoroquinolone (the S-(-)-enantiomer of nadifloxacin) approved by India's CDSCO in 2020 as Emrok (IV) and Emrok-O (oral, given as the prodrug alalevonadifloxacin). It is not FDA-approved. Its differentiated mechanism - preferential inhibition of DNA gyrase while retaining topoisomerase IV affinity - confers potent bactericidal activity against Gram-positive pathogens including MRSA, quinolone-resistant S. aureus, and hetero-/vancomycin-intermediate strains, with a narrow mutant selection window and very low resistance frequency. Potency is enhanced at acidic pH, favoring intracellular and abscess-environment activity, and it is not a substrate of the staphylococcal NorA efflux pump. It is approved for acute bacterial skin and skin-structure infections, including diabetic foot infection and concurrent bacteremia, in adults. High oral bioavailability (~90%) with matched IV/oral pharmacokinetics enables IV-to-oral step-down. Class fluoroquinolone warnings (tendinopathy, neuropathy, CNS effects, dysglycemia) apply.
indications: Acute bacterial skin and skin-structure infections (ABSSSI) in adults, including diabetic foot infections
ABSSSI with concurrent bacteremia caused by susceptible Gram-positive organisms (including MRSA and quinolone-resistant S. aureus)

dosage.d: 800 mg infused over 90 minutes every 12 hours
dosage.n: Typical course 7-14 days; do not give as rapid bolus
Course 7-14 days; ~90% bioavailability supports IV-to-oral switch

admin: IV: infuse over 90 minutes; avoid rapid or bolus injection
Do not co-infuse with other drugs or additives (compatibility unknown); flush a shared line with 0.9% saline before and after
Oral: swallow tablets whole with water; may be taken with or without food
Separate oral doses from antacids, iron, zinc, sucralfate, and multivitamins (give at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after)
A yellow color of the solution does not indicate loss of potency
moa: Levonadifloxacin is bactericidal through inhibition of bacterial type II topoisomerases, with strong preferential affinity for DNA gyrase while retaining significant topoisomerase IV affinity - in contrast to older fluoroquinolones that act largely via topoisomerase IV in Gram-positive organisms. This balanced, gyrase-preferential targeting underlies its activity against quinolone-resistant and methicillin-resistant S. aureus and its narrow mutant selection window with a very low frequency of resistant mutants. Antibacterial potency is enhanced at acidic pH, favoring intracellular killing and activity within abscesses and the diabetic-foot environment, and the molecule is not extruded by the staphylococcal NorA efflux pump. Its spectrum includes MRSA, quinolone-resistant and vancomycin-intermediate S. aureus, streptococci, enterococci, atypicals, and quinolone-susceptible Gram-negatives.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to levonadifloxacin or other quinolones
History of tendon disorders related to fluoroquinolone use
relative: Older age (>60), concurrent corticosteroids, or organ transplant (increased tendon risk)
History of CNS disorders or seizures
monitor: Diarrhea / signs of Clostridioides difficile infection

preg: Human data are lacking; animal studies were non-teratogenic at 7-10 times the human dose. The prescribing information lists levonadifloxacin as contraindicated in pregnancy.
lact: Levonadifloxacin is present in rat milk; excretion in human milk is unknown. The prescribing information lists it as contraindicated during lactation.
renal: No dedicated pharmacokinetic studies have been conducted in renal impairment and no dialysis-clearance data are available; the effect of renal impairment and any required dose adjustment are not established.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is recommended. Pharmacokinetics are unchanged in mild to moderate hepatic impairment, and even in severe impairment the AUC increase is less than 2-fold.

major: Antacids (magnesium/aluminium), sucralfate, iron, zinc, and multivitamins reduce oral absorption - separate by at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after the dose
moderate: No formal drug-interaction studies; IV compatibility with other agents is unknown - do not mix in the same line
minor: Low CYP450 interaction potential (midazolam, cyclosporine, warfarin, theophylline unlikely to be affected)
interactions.food: Oral levonadifloxacin may be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal delays Tmax and modestly lowers Cmax without clinically significant change in overall exposure.
interactions.alcohol: Not specifically addressed in labeling; general fluoroquinolone caution applies.

serious: CNS effects (seizures, raised intracranial pressure, toxic psychosis, depression/suicidal ideation)
emergency: Severe or bloody persistent diarrhea (C. difficile colitis)

monitoring: Diarrhea and signs of C. difficile infection
counsel: Take or receive the medicine every 12 hours and complete the full 7-14 day course even if you feel better
If taking the oral tablets, separate them from antacids, iron, zinc, sucralfate, and multivitamins (at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after)
Report tendon pain or swelling, numbness or tingling, mood changes, or severe/bloody diarrhea right away
Diabetic patients should monitor their blood sugar
This medicine is not for use in pregnancy, breastfeeding, or in those under 18 years
pk: Bactericidal; steady state by about day 2 of dosing
Plasma Tmax within a few hours of dosing
Dosed every 12 hours; no accumulation over 5 days
Store below 30 C, protect from light, keep in carton
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - approved only by India's CDSCO (Emrok IV, Emrok-O oral); use authoritative Indian prescribing information
Gyrase-preferential and not a NorA efflux substrate, so it retains activity against quinolone-resistant S. aureus and MRSA
Enhanced potency at acidic pH is relevant for abscesses, diabetic-foot, and intracellular S. aureus
~90% oral bioavailability with matched IV/oral PK enables early IV-to-oral step-down
Resistance frequency is very low; Phase III studies showed non-inferiority to linezolid in ABSSSI
missed: Not specified in labeling. General guidance: take a missed oral dose as soon as you remember; if it is almost time for the next 12-hourly dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Human overdose effects are not established; doses up to 2.4 g/day were tolerated by healthy volunteers. There is no specific antidote. Management is supportive with maintenance of hydration; dialysis clearance data are not available.
